subject: Staged micro-hotfix & escape-lane plan for Private fleet
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Aurelia Ops <ops@aureliahealth.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Staged micro-hotfix & escape-lane plan for Private fleet

Team —

We need to push a targeted micro-hotfix to a small subset of Private customers to address a tokenization edge-case that causes an elevated 5xx rate for long prompt batches. Aurelia reported a hit in production this morning (see inline). The plan must be low-risk: short maintenance window, version pin preserved for non-candidates, and a fast, automated rollback.

Asks in this thread:
- Can NetOps support a 30-minute narrow window tomorrow 0200-0230 PT for a canary slice (5 nodes) in us-west-2?
- Soojin, can you confirm the exact pinning logic we should use so non-canary fleets do not consume the new binaries?
- Vivek, please outline the minimal network gating steps and the abort criteria you want on monitoring.
- Rishi/Monica, please prepare a one-page rollback checklist and comms blurb for customers (Aurelia included).

Attachments: microhotfix_patch_notes_v1.2.pdf (notes), rollback_checklist.md (starter)

Background: internal telemetry shows the 5xx spikes correlate with long prompt KV cache growth + a pathological BOS token scenario. The patch is a 12-line change to tokenizer fallback; binary delta is ~3MB. This is intentionally small to minimize surface area.

I propose the following quick acceptance criteria for the canary:
- 15 minutes steady state with per-minute 5xx <= baseline + 0.2%
- No KV eviction errors in the logs
- Tail latency P99 does not increase more than 25ms

If acceptable, I'll schedule the slot and loop in Aurelia for a brief warning.

-Steph
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

---

Subject: Re: Staged micro-hotfix & escape-lane plan for Private fleet

SGTM. A few specifics from my side:

1) Version pinning: we should use a "pin-label" approach rather than permanent model-version blocking. Create a new pin-label "microfix-20280715" and apply it only to the 5 candidate instances. Existing pinning rules will keep the rest at their current binary. The pin-label is reversible via an API call so rollback can be immediate.

2) Binary rollout: upload delta to S3 (signed URL) and have the agent fetch with signature verification. Agent will perform an atomic swap of the tokenizer module to avoid restarting the whole process; fallback to previous module on hash mismatch.

3) KV cache considerations: we must warm the cache in the canary by replaying 10 typical requests to prime shapes used by Aurelia before the public window. That reduces cold-cache variance in the 15-minute steady-state baseline.

4) Instrumentation: add two short-lived telemetry meters scoped to the pin-label: tokenizer_errors.v2 and kv_eviction.warn. These will be emitted at 1s granularity for the canary window only.

5) Rollback: if any of the following occur, automatic rollback should trigger and leave the pin-label untouched for non-candidate fleets:
   - tokenizer_errors.v2 > 0 for 2 consecutive minutes
   - 5xx rate exceeds baseline + 0.5% for 5 consecutive minutes
   - manual abort from SRE on-call

I'll attach a short checklist and the agent fetch command.

- Soojin

I can cover network gating and the operational abort ladder. Notes below:

- Window: 2028-07-16 02:00-02:30 PT (as proposed). We'll reserve a narrow maintenance ACL so only the 5 node canary receives traffic.

- Traffic routing: use weighted routing at the edge with 0.0->1.0 ramp over 2 minutes then hold. If the telemetry shows regressions, we will drop traffic to 0 immediately and move traffic back to pinned hosts.

- Healthcheck and abort criteria (operational):
  * If per-minute 5xx spikes for the canary > baseline + 0.4% for 3 consecutive minutes -> auto-abort.
  * If connection reset or TLS handshake errors observed on >1 node -> immediate abort.

- Network rollback path: fail traffic at the load-balancer (edge router) and mark nodes as drained; we will not rely on node reboots. EdgeNet (cc'd) — please standby to remove the weighted route on request.

- Dry-run: we should rehearse the route flip in a staging environment prior to the window (3 hours earlier) to validate weighted routing scripts. Monica, can you own scheduling the rehearsal?

I'll create a short runbook snippet and push to the Drive folder in the related_links.

-Vivek

Thanks everyone — consolidated plan below and next steps. I added the small rollback checklist into the Drive folder.

Consolidated plan (short):
- Rehearsal in staging: 2028-07-16 23:00 PT (Monica to schedule)
- Canary maintenance window: 2028-07-16 02:00-02:30 PT (us-west-2, 5 nodes)
- Pre-warm: 02:00-02:05 run 10 sample requests per node
- Weighted ramp: 02:05-02:07 ramp from 0 -> target 100% for the canary slice, hold through 02:20
- Acceptance: 02:05-02:20 check telemetry (tokenizer_errors.v2 == 0, kv_eviction.warn <= baseline, per-minute 5xx <= baseline + 0.2%)
- Abort: immediate rollback if any auto-abort trigger fires (Vivek to flip route, EdgeNet to remove weight)
- Postmortem: quick 30-min bridge at 04:00 PT if anything abnormal observed.

Customer comms: short notification to Claire at Aurelia at 18:00 PT today confirming window + rollback guarantees. Template link in Drive.

Action items:
- Monica: create rehearsal calendar and staging ticket (due: today EOD).
- Soojin: finalize pre-warm script and telemetry meters (due: tonight).
- Vivek: stand by for route flip and prepare network abort CLI (due: rehearsal).
- Stephanie: send customer notification and attach rollback checklist (done after rehearsal scheduled).

Attachments: I've dropped rollback_checklist.md to the Drive folder and linked the calendar event: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=abcd1234

I'll mark this as green to schedule once Monica confirms rehearsal.

Thanks — Rishi
